Build group_id: the federated families in ein_relation

Source: R/md-groups.R
md_build_groups.Rd

Takes the connected components of the group_member edges in ein_relation and stores one row per EIN that belongs to a group, as the derived table entity_group. Two EINs are in the same family exactly when they share a group_id, so the question pfmatch/R/dyads.R recomputes per query - are these two candidates the same family? - becomes one join.

Usage

md_build_groups(con = NULL, max_iter = 100L)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

max_iter

Upper bound on label-propagation passes. Each pass moves the smallest EIN at least one hop, so this bounds the longest path in a component. The real edges converge in a handful; reaching the bound is an error, not a silent partial answer.

Value

Invisibly, a one-row data frame: edges, EINs, groups, the largest and median group size, and the passes taken.

Details

This is the cluster_id of REDUCTION.md section 6a, under the name the schema uses (PLAN.md section 4, GROUP-STRUCTURE-FINDINGS.md section 1).

Only group_member edges

related_entity and disregarded_entity edges never enter the components. Unioned in, they join the health-system and university sectors into one component of 117,869 EINs (RELATION-BUILD-PLAN.md). Those edges will feed a separate related_entity_id, which needs its own guard. Edges with no counterparty EIN (ein_b NULL) and self-loops are skipped.

Why components, not the GEN

A group exemption number cannot be the key: one logical group already spans several GENs (Lions 4, AAU 7, 4-H 12), and Rev. Proc. 2026-8 makes central organisations drop all but one ruling by 2027-01-22. A central EIN holding several GENs links them all, and a member listed under two parents joins their groups, which a GEN key would miss.

One bad edge joins two families, so evidence is ranked

Connected components are only as good as the weakest edge: a single member listed under two parents joins their groups. In the first full build that happened through self-reported evidence. A filer writes another group's GEN on line H(c), by typo or from an old ruling, and a high-school orchestra became a member of both a youth soccer league and Parent Booster USA. The result was one component of 25,739 EINs joining the US Catholic Conference, the Mayo Clinic, a sorority and a motorcycle club.

So each member's edges are filtered before the components are taken. Only its best-ranked evidence counts, in this order:

  1. bmf_group_exemption - the IRS's own coding.

  2. efile_affiliate_listing - the parent's own roster on its group return.

  3. nccs_group_metadata_historical - an older GEN assignment.

  4. efile_group_exemption_number - the member's own line H(c).

  5. anything else.

The first two are kept whole: a member the IRS or its parent places in two groups is a real link. From the self-reported ranks a member keeps one parent, the one it reported in the most filings (then the latest, then the smallest EIN). The set-aside edges stay in ein_relation; only the components ignore them.

How group_id is named

group_id is "GRP-" followed by the digits of the smallest EIN in the component, e.g. GRP-01-0347504. It depends only on the component's membership, so rebuilding gives the same ids, and adding an unrelated group moves no existing one - unlike a row number. It carries no other meaning: the smallest EIN is often a member, not the parent. Use group_central_ein for the parent.

Columns

ein

an EIN that appears in at least one group_member edge

group_id

the family, as above

group_size

EINs in the component

role

parent (only ever ein_a), member (only ever ein_b), or both - an EIN that is a parent in one edge and a member in another

n_parents

distinct parents this EIN is a member of; above 1 is what joins two stars into one family

group_central_ein

the parent with the most members in the component; ties go to the smallest EIN

EINs in no group get no row. A LEFT JOIN from entity gives them NULL.

Rebuild after any relation ingest

Like md_build_compact(), this drops and rebuilds. It reads only ein_relation, keyed on EIN rather than on reassigned row ids, so a re-ingest leaves it out of date rather than broken. Rebuild it after any ingest that writes group_member edges.
